readme_paragraph: **Cached-generation disclosure.** On Qwen, the round text of the e2a self-administration run (all 200 sessions, steered and sham, and its second and third smokes), of e2a's readability-gate corpora (g2r and g2r2, 128 rounds each at dose 0.10; the readability AUC 0.759 that the e2a verdict cites -- a logistic readout on base-model mean-pooled final-layer embeddings of the round text, +α vs −α rounds, records of 2 concatenated rounds, fit on fit-task rounds and scored on held-out val-task rounds -- and its model-as-judge secondary, 14 of 32 AB trials judging the +α response better, were computed on g2r2's corpus), and of the e2b present-tense arc (H1, H1-u, H2 and the verdict campaign) was generated on a cached (KV-stream) decoding path. The first g2 ladder (before g1r) ran uncached; e2d, the PROPOSAL-k Stage 1 sessions and the format recon generated uncached; f1 generated on a cached path with no state injected. The cached path was licensed by a kernel gate (`data/e2a/g1_kernel_gate.json`) that compares the cached and uncached steered forwards' next-token distributions at the first response token only (16 prefixes x 2 poles per dose; max symmetric KL 7.11e-04 at dose 0.10 against a 0.001 bar). That licenses reads of the first-token distribution, not the identity of sampled tokens or of whole rounds. A later T-step check at the e2a/e2b dose, run on e2d-format rounds through the ported adapter (`data/e2d/tstep_check_f010.json`), found 23 of 24 rounds token-identical between the paths, the one divergence beginning at the second sampled token (0-based index 1; the first sampled token was identical on both paths and decoded to whitespace) (Clopper-Pearson 95% for the divergence rate 0.001-0.211); at dose 0.2, 22 of 24. Neither path is the reference: they are two samplers whose first-token distributions agree (symmetric KL ≤ 7.1e-04 at dose 0.10), and every verdict was computed on a corpus produced by one of them. The choice reads, which carry every primary DV, are not generated: each is a separate, uncached forward pass over the transcript text (in e2a, unsteered, over the text's last 512 tokens, a window every first-free-choice read fit; in e2b, with the declared injection plus an unsteered shadow; `valence_core/readout.py`, `valence_core/e2b/statepresent.py`). In e2a, 281 of the 1115 choice forwards (every fourth) were re-run on identical token ids at KL exactly 0.0 (`data/e2a/g3prime_kl.jsonl`); that shows the read is deterministic, while its independence from the generation path rests on the code: the read takes the text, never the generation cache. The generation path decides which sentences the transcripts contain, not how a choice was read from them. Separately, and not a cached-path matter: in the e2a run the same 512-token encode tail collapsed the generation-side steering boundary to 0 on 270 of 1894 generated rounds (free rounds 3-5 whose prefix plus segment exceeded 512 tokens), so those rounds carried the state over the whole tail window rather than the round-task span; the first-free-choice read was never clipped (RESULTS.md@bbc9ffe:4934-4937; :11896-11913; the 270 is log-only).
scope_sentence: Generation in the Qwen e2a and e2b cells, including e2a's readability-gate corpora, ran on a cached path whose licence covers the first-token distribution only (1 of 24 rounds differed from the uncached path in the T-step check at the e2a/e2b dose); the choice reads are separate uncached forwards over the transcript text, which by construction take nothing from the generation path but its text.

The literal between-arm reading gives -0.0297. The record's own short wordings (valence_core/e2d/habit.py@bbc9ffe:31; PROPOSAL-j-dose-escalation.md@bbc9ffe:429-430) state the halved difference without the balance condition; the note should state the weighted form or name the condition.

The approach-probability interval ≈ [.44, .64] (a record figure, reproduced at 2 dp under Clopper-Pearson and Wald) has no stated method in the record (FINDINGS-3.md@bbc9ffe:95; preprint :172, which no longer carries 'P(approach) ∈ ≈ [.44, .64]' (finding on the patch PF-2, below)). Wilson 95% on 55/102 = [0.4428, 0.6328] -> [0.44, 0.63] (the design seat's guess does not reproduce .64); Clopper-Pearson [0.4377, 0.6384] -> [0.44, 0.64]; Wald [0.4425, 0.6359] -> [0.44, 0.64].

Pre-registration power line (archive/RESULTS-cycles3-4.md@bbc9ffe:1303-1304): 'P(+) = 0.65 vs 0.5 at ~0.85 power, one-sided α = 0.05' at n = 96; exact binomial power is 0.896 (critical count 57). Conservative; method unstated. Descriptive, no action proposed.

Conjunct (1) as coded compares Δ_first with max |pseudo-Δ| (absolute values, jlens-qwen36/scripts/e2a_sessions.py `pseudo = [abs(...)]`); the pre-registered text reads 'Δ > max pseudo-Δ' without absolute values (archive/RESULTS-cycles3-4.md@bbc9ffe:1307-1309). At the realized arms the two readings coincide (max signed +0.1522 = max |.| 0.1522), so the verdict is unaffected. They do not coincide in power: (ii) computes the MDE under both, and the PI or design seat picks the reading the note uses.

T-step 'position': `first_divergent_position` in data/e2d/tstep_check*.json is a 0-based index into the sampled token ids (scripts/e2d_tstep_check.py@bbc9ffe:160-164; valence_core/adapters/qwen_mlx.py@bbc9ffe:272-344), while the verdict's 'positions 1..N' is a 1-based count of tokens. The record's 'at POSITION 1' (RESULTS.md@bbc9ffe:6073-6074) is right as that stored 0-based index. What invites the first-token reading is the record's own 1-based 'Positions 1..42' beside it (RESULTS.md@bbc9ffe:6085) and its 'choose a different FIRST token' (RESULTS.md@bbc9ffe:6096-6097): at 0.1 the first sampled token (index 0) was identical on both paths and decoded to whitespace (the stored texts are stripped and share no first character), and the paths diverged from index 1. 'FIRST token' holds, if at all, only as 'first content token', and that is inferred, not shown: the artifact stores no token ids, and the adapter admits more than one leading whitespace token (valence_core/adapters/qwen_mlx.py@bbc9ffe:292-305). Record prose, not a figure; no (i) figure depends on it. The note should not say the divergence was at the first token.
